chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: There is no manumission for the believer after death.
Nor is there a postponement of his debt.
Nor is there division of his inheritances.
Except if he has a debt, or inheritance, or manumission that was determined before death.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a deceased person's debts and inheritances in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (a) clarification that posthumous estate distribution is strictly bound by pre-death determinations, ensuring legal certainty in inheritance and debt settlement. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the deceased’s final will and settled obligations take precedence, preventing arbitrary changes to the estate’s allocation after death. It highlights the importance of timely settlement of *haqq al-nas* (rights of people) before the transition to the afterlife.
